Nora: Ran into a weird parity issue with the Next agent starter (LangChain-ish wiring) when deployed to edge: agent actions sometimes never stream back and the eval harness times out.
Diego: Can you share repro steps?
Nora: Repo: github.com/redwood/sample-agent-next, branch edge-demo. Build with next@13.5 edge runtime, set RW_KEY, then hit /api/agent via curl. Sometimes the response stays pending for 30s then the harness fails. Locally on node runtime it's rock solid.
Hannah: Any errors in Vercel logs?
Nora: Logs show early 502s followed by retry success. Also saw: 
```
WARN: SDK: stream closed before first chunk
Error: Eval harness timed out waiting for stream
    at evalHarness (/workspace/eval/index.js:78:12)
```
Olga: Streaming on edge uses TransformStream. Our SDK provides a Node stream polyfill for examples. Maybe the bundle includes both and the runtime picks the wrong impl.
Diego: Also we recently changed retry semantics to use exponential backoff with jitter; that relies on setTimeout and performance.now. Edge runtimes sometimes have different timer behaviors.
Nora: I instrumented the sample: when stream fails, the SDK had promised the stream but never flushed headers. Looks like init() returned before the streaming transport finished setup.
Hannah: Did you call await init(...) in the handler?
Nora: No, sample used init() without await to keep examples terse.
Olga: That's likely it. On Node the module cache makes init effectively warm, on edge cold starts expose the race. We should update samples to show await init and add a comment about edge cold start.
Diego: For parity, SDK should make init idempotent and expose a sync-safe check like isReady() so callers can await or gate requests. Also ensure our streaming transport falls back to native TransformStream if available.
Nora: I pushed a tiny change in my fork that switches the sample to: 
```js
export default async function handler(req) {
  await init({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
  const res = await agent.run(req.body)
  return new Response(res.body)
}
```
Diego: Nice. Can you add a comment explaining why await is necessary on edge?
Nora: Will do. Also opened an SDK issue to detect dual stream polyfills and prefer the platform native one: #SRV-411.
Hannah: CI-bot: I added a flaky test QA case for edge streaming (flaky-agent-streaming).
ci-bot: Created ticket CI-4479 and queued a reproducibility job.
Olga: We'll also add a small unit test in SDK that simulates missing setTimeout and missing global fetch to ensure graceful fallback for retries and telemetry.
Diego: Timeline?
Olga: I'll draft the SDK PR tomorrow; Nora's sample PR patches docs immediately.
Nora: Patch link: https://github.com/redwood/sample-agent-next/pull/22 — updates handler + README note. I'll verify on Vercel once PR merges.
Diego: Great. Thanks for the repro.
Nora: :thumbsup:
